variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: architectural MODEL MOCKUP for a Smart Home chapter in an existing electrician website, direction A: bedroom and balcony room control.
Input image 1 is the exact existing upper-floor Blender model and the primary geometry/reference anchor. Input image 2 is the same house exterior, supporting material/balcony reference only.
Create ONE polished square architectural 3D cutaway visualization, on pure white, of this SAME model with a closer, lower oblique camera focusing on the front-left parents' bedroom, its balcony and the adjoining central hallway. Think a camera push-in within the existing scene, not a new room design. The parents' bedroom has a double bed against the left wall, the existing broad oak wardrobe on the back wall, warm white bedding, and front-facing floor-to-ceiling oak-framed balcony glazing. Preserve the balcony's black vertical metal railings, tiled floor, small chair and round table. Keep a believable slice of the existing central hall and stair opening toward the rear right as spatial context; neighboring rooms can lie outside the crop. No roof, no new storey, no rearrangement of the house.
Proposed smart-home additions: a physically small, premium graphite wall-mounted room controller beside the bedroom door in the central hallway at realistic switch height, with a discreet warm-white temperature display; slim exterior venetian blind slats at the balcony glazing, partly lowered with slats tilted open so the oak window and bedroom remain readable; a subtle ceiling-mounted presence sensor near the bedroom entrance. Show the controller visibly, correctly attached to a wall facing the camera. All existing bedside and ambient lamps already on, warm and restrained. The view should communicate comfortable automatic shading and room control through real modeled devices, not through a magical light show.
Composition: bedroom, balcony and controller form one clear focal area, fill roughly 82 percent of the square; tasteful studio soft shadows, the same cream plaster, natural oak and anthracite materials as the source, physically plausible high-quality Blender/Cycles appearance with crisp thin railings.
NO infographic labels, captions, letters, floating cards, app screens, tablet mockups, cables drawn in the air, glowing network webs, people, logos or watermarks. The tiny controller may display only 21°. Do not invent a new house or alter door/window locations. This is a conceptual addition to the provided architecture, not a finished native render.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: architectural MODEL MOCKUP for the Smart Home chapter of an electrician website, direction B: living room comfort scene.
Input image 1 is the existing ground-floor Blender cutaway and the PRIMARY geometry anchor. Input image 2 is the same house exterior and supports accurate oak glazing, terrace and material identity only.
Create ONE polished square architectural 3D visualization of THIS SAME HOUSE'S front-left living room, open dining area and existing adjacent entrance. Use a much closer oblique cutaway view, still from the front looking into the house, framing the sofa, dining area, front oak-framed terrace glazing, part of the terrace and the hallway wall at right; the kitchen and central U-shaped stair should remain recognizable in the upper background. Keep the original L-sofa against the left wall with chaise front-left, wood coffee table, oval six-chair dining table behind the sofa, oak kitchen at rear left, central stair and front-right oak entrance door. The house plan and circulation must stay unchanged; do not create a new apartment.
Proposed smart-home elements: a small realistic graphite scene keypad with a discrete temperature display mounted on the living-room-facing side of the existing short wall between the living area and entrance hall at right; slim anthracite exterior venetian blinds on the existing large front terrace glazing, lowered only through the upper third so you can still see the terrace and oak frame; a tiny ceiling presence sensor at the circulation edge. The controller should be readable as a physical device at normal switch height. Existing reading lamp and dining pendant warmly on; all illumination already on in every chapter. A cozy homecoming or comfortable evening scene, warm neutral daylight and restrained indoor illumination, no dark night background.
Composition: terrace at lower left, cozy sofa center-left, keypad wall center-right; focus on control + visible shading response within a real room. Pure white studio background around clean cut geometry, cream plaster, light oak, cream furniture, muted olive sofa cushions and thin anthracite accents match the original. Refined realistic Blender/Cycles architectural model, softly shaded and carefully proportioned.
NO infographic labels, floating screens, captions, title lettering, smartphone mockups, giant controls, glowing trails, orange network webs, exaggerated colored lighting, extra furniture, people, logos or watermarks. Device display may say only 21°. Preserve recognizable source geometry and furniture arrangement.
variants.correctionPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the supplied living-room Smart Home architectural mockup.
Make ONE localized correction to the physical smart room controller. Remove the small black 21° controller from the OUTSIDE front facade beside the exterior front door at the lower-right. Restore plain cream plaster there with no device. Relocate that same physically small graphite 21° room controller to the existing INSIDE left-side living-room wall, beside the side window with blinds, below the framed art toward the dining area, at normal switch height above the sofa arm. It must read unmistakably as an interior device reachable from the living room. Correct perspective so it lies flush on that left interior wall.
Keep everything else exactly the same: camera, image crop, original house geometry, both window blinds, all existing furniture and exact furniture positions, kitchen, stairs, terrace, door, warm light, wood window frames, cream and oak materials, white background. Do not add UI callouts, arrows, labels, people, other devices, new walls or new architecture. No other changes.
